name: Startups
metaTitle: HR and hiring for startups | Hirebrew
metaDescription: Build a repeatable hiring and onboarding rhythm with Hirebrew. Explore candidate conversations, structured interviews and a clearer first month for your team.
headline: Build your team. Keep your momentum.
subhead: Give every new hire a clear journey, without making your growing company feel like a big-company process.
summary: A repeatable hiring and onboarding rhythm for your next stage.
challengeTitle: Your next hire should not need another spreadsheet.
challenge: In a small company, the founder approves the role, a team lead interviews and someone in operations organises day one. When those handoffs live in separate conversations, candidates wait and new starters arrive without a plan. Hirebrew brings the people journey into focus, so a lean team can establish a useful operating rhythm early.

priorities.title: Hire with a shared brief

priorities.title: Keep the conversation moving
priorities.body: Explore a candidate pipeline with two-way messages. Candidates can respond, and the hiring team can see what needs attention next.

priorities.title: Make the first month count
priorities.body: Connect onboarding tasks, manager ownership and early goals. A small team still deserves a considered welcome and clear expectations.

workflowTitle: From an open role to a confident start.
workflowIntro: Start with the next role you genuinely need. Keep the process small enough for everyone involved to understand and use.

steps.label: Define
steps.title: Approve a real business need
steps.body: Capture the purpose of the role, decision owner and interview criteria before sourcing begins. Avoid changing the brief halfway through selection.

steps.label: Connect
steps.title: Keep both sides informed
steps.body: Follow candidate stages and exchange messages around the next step. Test the experience from the candidate's side, not only the recruiter's.

steps.label: Decide
steps.title: Compare evidence, not memory
steps.body: Bring interviewers into the process and collect structured scorecards. Keep the final hiring decision with the people responsible for the role.

steps.label: Welcome
steps.title: Carry the context into day one
steps.body: Assign first-week tasks and a first-month plan. Make introductions, responsibilities and the first check-in explicit before the new hire starts.

pilot.title: Prove the rhythm with one role.

challengeTitle: The right review happens before the rollout.
challenge: People systems touch sensitive information, employment decisions and documents that carry real consequences. Legal teams need more than a generic compliance badge: they need to know what information is collected, who can use it and what happens next. Hirebrew's evaluation approach makes those questions part of workflow design, with clear boundaries between a useful process and a verified control.

pilot.boundary: Use the prototype to shape the process. Live personal data, identity, notifications and any AI provider require separate readiness checks.

faqs.q: How is this different from the startup solution?
faqs.a: The startup page focuses on a small company's operating rhythm. This founder view focuses on making your context explicit, delegating responsibly and helping managers take ownership as the company grows.

faqs.q: Can I keep visibility without owning every task?
faqs.a: That is the process to evaluate: named role owners, visible stages and agreed check-ins. Test the manager and founder information needs rather than assuming everyone needs access to everything.
Follow your next meaningful hire from approval through the first month. Document where the journey still depends on you, then assign a clear owner or decision rule.
